title: Restore alert detection and notification, and monitor the alerting system itself

sha_binding.verified_source_note: Exact committed lane source carrying the five PM-required corrections and the fixes for the defects an independent adversarial review found in the first attempt at them. The two earlier correction commits were rewritten into this one because a commit message referenced a second issue, which branch discipline refuses. Later commits are restricted to proof artifacts. Post-merge closeout rebinds the proof to the authoritative merge SHA.

focused_tests.detail: 17 node:test cases: line-movement detection and persistence, live-mode canary notification, alerting silence, stale ingestion, failed delivery, unknown monitor state, workflow posture, observed-cadence threshold calibration in both directions, the production threshold floor honouring operator values above it, member-target withholding, transport-level member refusal, fail-closed behaviour on an unresolvable target map, non-message requests passing through, undelivered-detection retry built from a real alert_detections row shape, and an end-to-end alert-worthy pass proving canary delivery with the member channel withheld.

verify_static.detail: Environment checks, policy checks, lint, type-check, build, aggregate tests, Smart Form verification, and command verification passed.

pnpm_verify.detail: The full static stage passed. The final writable DB stage refused the workstation loopback target before executing DB tests, as required for a T1 lane.

r_level_check.detail: 9 changed files; no R-level rules matched and no R-level artifacts are required for this diff.

member_channel_guard.policy: Member-facing alert delivery is unauthorized. The safe default is canary-only; member channels require a separate activation decision via ALERT_MEMBER_CHANNELS_ENABLED=true.
member_channel_guard.fixture: NBA spread moved from 4.5 to 9.0 (above the 3.5 alert-worthy threshold) with BOTH discord:canary and discord:trader-insights resolvable in the target map, so the member channel was genuinely reachable and only the guard prevented delivery.
observed: every outbound Discord request went to canary channel 1296531122234327100; none reached member channel 1296531122234327999
notification.failed = 0 and notification.notified = 1: a refused member channel is a policy decision, not a delivery failure, so the detection is not left unnotified and re-queued indefinitely
detection persisted at tier alert-worthy, marked notified, notified_channels = ['discord:canary']
the alert.notification run recorded a non-zero blockedMemberDeliveries, leaving a durable trace of the refusal
guard fails closed: when the target map cannot be resolved, no channel is permitted
member_channel_guard.validated_by_inversion: With the activation check flipped so the guard returns the raw fetch, 3 tests fail and name the breach: "member channel was contacted: .../channels/1296531122234327100/messages, .../channels/1296531122234327999/messages". Restoring the guard returns the suite to 15 passed, 0 failed. The control was proven by making it fail, not by its presence.
enforcement_layers: primary: applyMemberChannelPolicy strips every non-canary entry from UNIT_TALK_DISCORD_TARGET_MAP unless ALERT_MEMBER_CHANNELS_ENABLED=true, so the delivery loop skips the member channel with no attempt, no retry ladder, and no audit rows
defence in depth: buildChannelGuardedFetch throws on any Discord message POST to a non-canary channel and fails closed when the target map cannot be resolved
member_channel_guard.known_limitation: Enforced in this script only. packages/alert-runtime/src/alert-agent.ts calls runAlertNotificationPass with no injected fetchImpl, so apps/alert-agent would deliver to discord:trader-insights unguarded. That path is dormant (last alert.detection run 2026-04-28). Making the policy a system property requires changing resolveChannels, which is outside this lane's scope.
member_channel_guard.cost_defect_corrected: An earlier revision enforced this only at the transport. A refused channel then burned the full retry ladder — four attempts and seven seconds of real sleep per detection — so roughly 86 alert-worthy detections would exhaust timeout-minutes: 10. The counter also counted attempts rather than distinct channels, reading 4x high.

undelivered_retry.defect: A detection persisted while Discord was unavailable collided with its idempotency key on later passes and was counted as a duplicate rather than returned in persistedSignals, so it was never retried after Discord recovered.
observed: mergeUndeliveredDetections re-submits recent detections whose notified flag is false
a detection already present in the current pass is not duplicated
a detection already delivered (notified true) is not resent
a detection outside the four-hour retry window is not resent
a retry-lookup failure cannot suppress the current pass's own alerts
undelivered_retry.corrected_defect: An earlier revision filtered on a `detected_at` field. `alert_detections` has no such column (verified against packages/db/src/database.types.ts: the row exposes created_at, current_snapshot_at, baseline_snapshot_at). Every candidate therefore failed Date.parse and the retry silently returned zero. It now reads `created_at` with no cast, so the type system enforces the field, and the test fixture is built from a real AlertDetectionRecord instead of a hand-written shape.
undelivered_retry.runtime_measurement: A probe persisted one genuinely undelivered alert-worthy detection via saveDetection and called the shipped function: rows=1, has created_at=true, notified=false, RETRIED COUNT = 1. The same probe measured 0 before this correction.

threshold_calibration.rationale: The workflow is scheduled */5 but eight consecutive production runs were measured 18-49 minutes apart (gaps 20/29/36/49/18/24/21, effective cadence near 28). The previous nominal-5 clamp would mark a healthy system CRITICAL on nearly every pass once ingestion resumes.
threshold_calibration.change: offers and cycle clamp to a 60-minute observed-cadence FLOOR under --production-cadence, honouring larger operator values above it. The workflow's ALERT_SYSTEM_STALE_MINUTES default was also corrected from 15 to 60, because the alert.detection/alert.notification runs that threshold watches are produced by the same throttled scheduler.
observed: a six-minute-old offer is not CRITICAL
a ninety-minute-old offer is CRITICAL at threshold 60m
a value below the floor is raised to 60; a value above it (120) is honoured, so the env knob is not disabled
threshold_calibration.supersedes: Item 3 of UTV2-1738, which recorded this as an untuned follow-up.
threshold_calibration.corrected_defect: An earlier revision computed Math.max(Math.min(x, 5), 60), which is always exactly 60 and silently disabled both UNIT_TALK_INGESTOR_OFFER_STALE_MINUTES and INGESTOR_ALERT_CYCLE_THRESHOLD_MINUTES. The workflow also still pinned ALERT_SYSTEM_STALE_MINUTES to 15, making the previous 60-minute self-monitor claim false at that head.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: Alert detection and notification run on a production cadence.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: The workflow runs a live-mode scheduled alerting pass before the monitor job. The */5 schedule is not honoured under load; measured effective cadence is roughly 28 minutes, and thresholds are calibrated to that observed cadence rather than the nominal one.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: Alerting system silence and delivery failures are observable.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: The monitor checks persisted alert.detection and alert.notification runs and treats missing/stale/failed receipts as CRITICAL. Scope stated precisely: the monitor is needs: alerting-pass inside the same workflow run, so always() grants independence from that job's OUTCOME, not from the SCHEDULE. It is structurally blind to the scheduler never dispatching at all (precedent: UTV2-1517). External scheduler-death detection is out of scope here and owned by UTV2-1738.
Merged offer freshness reads provider_cycle_status.updated_at; result freshness reads game_results.created_at; no provider_offers.updated_at query remains in the workflow script.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: The repaired alert path is executable without enabling autonomous system picks.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: ALERT_DRY_RUN is false for delivery, SYSTEM_PICKS_ENABLED remains false, and the focused test observes persisted detection and notification behavior.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: Writable T1 verification runs only against governed staging credentials.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: The local staging identity guard refused host 127.0.0.1 before any writable DB test ran.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: Member-facing alert delivery remains unauthorized; the safe default is canary-only.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: buildChannelGuardedFetch refuses every Discord channel except the resolved canary unless ALERT_MEMBER_CHANNELS_ENABLED=true. This lane sets that variable nowhere. Proven by inversion; see runtime_proof.member_channel_guard.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: Persisted-but-undelivered alerts are retried without duplicating successful deliveries.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: mergeUndeliveredDetections re-submits recent detections with notified=false, excluding those already in the pass, already delivered, or outside the retry window. See runtime_proof.undelivered_retry.

acceptance_criteria_mapping.criterion: Thresholds are calibrated against the observed scheduler cadence to prevent routine false CRITICALs.
acceptance_criteria_mapping.evidence: Production thresholds clamp to a 60-minute observed-cadence floor. See runtime_proof.threshold_calibration.

corrections_applied: member-facing routing is explicitly opt-in and blocked by default in two layers
persisted-but-undelivered alerts are retried without duplicating successful deliveries, reading the real created_at column (measured RETRIED COUNT = 1; it was 0 before)
thresholds calibrated to the observed scheduler cadence as a floor that does not disable operator knobs, including the workflow's ALERT_SYSTEM_STALE_MINUTES default
self-monitor described accurately, including its same-run tautology; UTV2-1738 owns external scheduler-death detection

sign_off.independent_review_defects_fixed: An independent adversarial review at the preceding head 3b9dfd4b (since rewritten) returned CHANGES_REQUIRED with five blockers. All five are fixed at this head: the dead retry column, its self-confirming test fixture, the workflow pinning the self-monitor threshold to 15, the un-recomputed evidence counts, and a stale contradictory Safety posture section. Two follow-ups (the constant threshold expression and the retry-ladder cost) are also fixed; the alert-agent entry point and lane classification are disclosed as known limitations.
